newsitem.title: UK: W.Africa, UK/Cont tankers to firm further - brokers.
newsitem.headline: W.Africa, UK/Cont tankers to firm further - brokers.

text.p: West African-U.S. and inter-U.K./Cont tanker fixings firmed on Tuesday and look set to rise further, with the Caribbean also looking bullish due to bad weather, brokers said.
"West Africa and the North Sea are the ones to watch," a London broker said.
"West Africa's definitely getting busy. We're seeing W85-87.5 for 130,000 tonnes, a couple of points up from Monday, depending on dates, and next week we could be in the 90s."
But he pegged 260,000 tonnes on this route at about W62.5, little changed from Monday.

Another broker said 80,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont was being fixed at W110, well up from around W100 seen on Monday. "There's a lot of activity and a lack of tonnage," he added. "If this carries on it could move up to 115."

Transatlantic rates were seen slipping. "I've seen 80,000 (tonnes) at W115, against W125 not long ago...There's no great shortage of vessels and rates could come off a little bit," said a New York broker.

Middle East rates were flat, with W52.5-55 seen fixed for Mideast-west voyages for 250,000 tonne vessels. "There's quite a lot of tonnage around but you might get a slightly better price for a newer ship," one broker said.

A fourth tanker was fixed to load Iraqi crude from Mina al-Bakr, the Berge Bragd with 290,000 tonnes to the U.K./Cont for Bayoil at W55. The Berge Bragd is the second tanker that Bayoil has chartered from Mina al-Bakr since Iraqi oil exports resumed last month.
